title: Purification and cryoelectron microscopy structure determination of human V-ATPase
protocol: Transform the recombinant plasmid of pET28a containing flag-tagged SidK into E. coli BL21(DE3) RIPL.
Grow single colonies on an LB plate with 50 μg/mL Kanamycin.
Inoculate a single colony to 25 mL LB broth with 50 μg/mL Kanamycin for overnight culture at 37°C with shaking at 200 rpm.
Dilute the 25 mL culture into 1 L LB broth with 50 μg/mL Kanamycin and grow at 37°C with shaking at 200 rpm to a density of OD ~0.6.
Add 0.5 mM IPTG to the culture for induction of protein expression at 18°C for 16–20 hours.
Harvest the cultured cells by centrifugation at 180 rcf for 10 minutes.
Resuspend harvested cells in 30 mL buffer A at 4°C.
Disrupt cells by sonication (50% power, 5 s on, 5 s off) for 4 min on ice.
Centrifuge the cell lysate at 20,000 rcf for 40 min to remove debris.
Incubate supernatant with 1 mL Ni-NTA resin pre-equilibrated in buffer A at 4°C for 30 min.
Wash the resin with 10 mL of buffer A containing 20 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5, 300 mM NaCl, and 20 mM Imidazole.
Elute protein using 4 mL buffer B containing 20 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5, 300 mM NaCl, and 300 mM Imidazole.
Purify eluted flag-tagged SidK by gel filtration in buffer C containing 20 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, and 1 mM TCEP.
Analyze purity of the protein by SDS-PAGE.
Pool protein fractions and concentrate to 2 mg/mL using a spin filter concentrator.
Quantify protein concentration by measuring UV280 absorbance using NanoDrop Spectrophotometer.
Freeze 100 μL aliquots of SidK protein in liquid nitrogen.
Store frozen protein at -80°C.
Dilute one vial of frozen 293S cells into 25 mL Freestyle 293 medium and centrifuge at 180 rcf for 5 min.
Resuspend the cell pellets using 30 mL fresh medium supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% antibiotics-antimycotic in a 200 mL baffled flask.
Culture cells at 37°C with shaking at 100 rpm when the density is 2.0 million/mL.
Harvest 293S cells by centrifugation at 180 rcf for 10 min.
Resuspend harvested cells in 150 mL buffer D containing 50 mM HEPES, pH 7.5, 50 mM NaCl supplemented with protease inhibitor cocktail and incubate on ice for 2 h.
Further disrupt the cells by hand-driven Dounce homogenization.
Centrifuge cell lysate at 20,000 rcf for 30 min to remove cell debris.
Centrifuge the supernatant at 200,000 rcf in a Type 45 Ti rotor for 1 hour to obtain the membrane pellet.
Resuspend the membrane pellet in buffer E containing specified components and homogenize using a hand-driven Dounce homogenizer.
Mix the homogenized membrane solution with 0.1 mg flag-tagged SidK protein and incubate at 4°C for 4 hours.
Centrifuge the mixture at 20,000 rcf for 30 minutes to remove insoluble material.
Incubate the supernatant containing solubilized V-ATPase/SidK complex with 1 mL anti-Flag resin for 1 hour at 4°C.
Collect the resin and wash it with 10 mL buffer F containing specified components.
Elute the V-ATPase/SidK complex using 5 mL of buffer F plus 100 μg/mL 3X FLAG peptide.
Prepare 1 mL each of 15%, 30%, 45%, and 60% glycerol solutions in buffer G plus 0.001% lauryl maltose neopentyl glycol (LMNG) and 0.0001% cholesteryl hemisuccinate CHS.
Gently inject 1 mL of each glycerol solution (15%, 30%, 45%, and 60%) into the bottom of a polyclear centrifuge tube using a 1 mL syringe.
Slowly load between 100 μL and 500 μL V-ATPase fraction from the previous step on top of the glycerol gradient.
Balance the two tubes before loading them into the swing-out rotor.
Centrifuge at 171,520 rcf in a Beckman MLS-50 rotor and Beckman Optima MAX ultracentrifuge for 20 h at 4°C.
Manually fractionate by poking a hole at the bottom of the centrifuge tube after centrifugation.
Collect the first 16 fractions of 250 μL each during manual fractionation.
Analyze each fraction by SDS-PAGE to select the fractions with intact V-ATPase.
Quantify the V-ATPase concentration in selected fractions using a NanoDrop Spectrophotometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific).
Avoid air bubbles and disturb interfaces when loading glycerol into the centrifuge tube.
Do not boil samples for SDS-PAGE to prevent protein complex formation of large aggregates.
Glow-discharge copper grids for 1 minute at 30 mA current.
Apply a 3 μL drop of purified human V-ATPase sample to the glow-discharged grids.
Incubate the grids at 4°C for 10 minutes.
Wash the grids three times using 5 μL buffer G containing 20 mM HEPES and 150 mM NaCl.
Blot the grids using standard vitrobot filter paper with a force of 5 for 4 seconds in 100% humidity at 4°C.
Plunge the grids into liquid ethane using an FEI Vitrobot Mark IV.
Save grids with good ice and particle distribution for data collection.
Load grids to FEI Titan Krios microscope with a K3 detector and energy filter.
Collect data in counting mode, taking 40 frames per movie in 3.2 seconds.
Ensure a total dose of 50 electrons per Å² during data collection.
Use a physical pixel size of 1.08 Å for imaging.
Set defocus values between 1 nm to 3 nm.
Wash samples three times to eliminate glycerol before grid preparation.
Store prepared grids in liquid nitrogen if not used immediately for screening and data collection.
Process cryo-EM data to obtain cryo-EM density maps of human V-ATPase.
Perform beam-induced motion correction using RELION and UCSF MOTIONCOR2.
Estimate contrast transfer function using CTFFIND4.1 in RELION.
Select initial particles using a template-free auto-picking procedure based on a Laplacian-of-Gaussian filter.
Perform 2D classification of selected particles to generate templates for further picking.
Use Gautomatch with the generated templates as references for particle picking.
Pickle total 782,583 particles for 2D classification.
Select good classes from 2D classification for subsequent 3D classification.
Classify selected particles into 6 classes in 3D classification.
Refine three states of V-ATPase using non-uniform 3D refinement in cryoSPARC.
Obtain three maps with resolutions of 3.1 Å, 3.4 Å, and 3.6 Å from the refined states.
Build atomic models based on obtained cryo-EM maps.
Generate an initial structure model of human V-ATPase using SWISS-MODEL based on yeast V-ATPase.
Fit the generated structures into cryo-EM maps as rigid bodies using Chimera.
Manually adjust the structures in Coot.
Perform real-space refinement using PHENIX.
Validate the models using PHENIX.
